REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - JULY 14, 2016 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
COUNCIL CHAMBERS, BLOOMFIELD AVENUE AT 183RD STREET
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON

BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Councilmember Jim Edwards.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by “The Justice League,” a Recreation Services
  Division Youth Soccer League PeeWee Division team.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Carol Chen
  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair George Ray

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  Proclamations were presented as follows:

  Marjorie M. Rosenberg (100th Birthday Celebration)

  Delores and Ronald Eveland (50th Wedding Anniversary)

  Rushabh Doshi (Outstanding Academic Achievements)

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Kerry Bossin spoke regarding budget cuts discussed at the last City Council
  meeting.

  Sarah Ambrose, Community Manager, spoke regarding the Relay for Life event.

  Ram Kakkar spoke regarding looping in City facilities.

  EXISTING SHOWROOM AND SERVICE CANOPY; A REMODEL OF THE

  (COUNCIL).

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for construction of street
  improvements in residential streets, Project No. 14088, Bid No. 1250-16
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Public Works Director.  A
  PowerPoint Presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Chen, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Award a contract in the amount of $546,563 for Residential Street Rehabilitation
  Program, Project No. 14088, Bid No. 1250-16, to Sequel Contractors and reject all
  other bids; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related change
  orders; and
  3. Authorize staff to utilize any remaining unexpended funding from Capital Project
  Nos. 14088 and 13057 for infrastructure improvements in the current fiscal year
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration to waive reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS IMPLEMENTING REVISED WATER
  CONSERVATION REGULATIONS (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vince Brar, Senior Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.
 City of Cerritos  July 14, 2016

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Chen, and seconded by Edwards, to waive full reading of

  OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS IMPLEMENTING REVISED WATER
  CONSERVATION REGULATIONS (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of the City of Cerritos 2016 Public Health Goal
  Assessment (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vince Brar, Senior Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Pulido, to direct staff to send
  confirmation to the regulatory agencies that the report has been completed and a
  public hearing has been held (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9D.  Review and consideration of a contract for professional construction
  management multi-prime services for the Cerritos Astor Museum project
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works.

  Marlene Rofe inquired as to the costs of the museum.

  Paul Bellenbaum spoke regarding the storage of cars at the museum.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
  speak, the Mayor closed public comments.
 City of Cerritos  July 14, 2016
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 7 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9D.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Chen, to:

  1. Reject the sole proposal received for construction management multi-prime
  services; and
  2. Authorize City staff to negotiate on the open market for construction management
  multi-prime services and to return to the City Council for award of contract
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Edwards, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9E.  Review and consideration of the City’s red light camera program (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works.
  Sheriff’s Deputy Tim Britt also participated in the staff report.  Director
  Vancheswaran noted that written correspondence was received on this item and
  copies were available in the Office of the City Clerk.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Jim Lissner spoke in opposition to the red light camera program.

  Paul Bellenbaum spoke in opposition to the red light camera program.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed public
  comments.

  A motion made by Edwards, and seconded by Chen, to go out to bid on the red
  light camera program did not pass (2 – 3, Pulido, Solanki, Ray “no”) due to lack
  of majority support.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Pulido, to terminate the
  existing red light camera program (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Chen, Pulido, Solanki, Ray
  NOES:  Edwards
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  A brief PowerPoint was displayed highlighting several City capital projects by
  Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works.
